summary: CCC-built 1937 tower in Bays Mountain Park, also called Garden Mountain or ET-12; climbable only on a capped Visit Kingsport hike (registration full when checked); height and county records disagree.

facts.design: steel tower with a seven-foot-square lookout shelter (1953 account)

access.note: Inside Bays Mountain Park. Visit Kingsport listed a capped early-arrival hike (12 places; registration full when checked) that includes going up inside the tower. No general climbing access found.

visit.trail_note: About 3.3 miles round trip on the Visit Kingsport early-arrival hike; the last stretch is steep with steps and switchbacks; the tower is not ADA compliant

facts.agency: Tennessee Division of Forestry operated it; City of Kingsport administers the site

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (NHLR; Bays Mountain History)
George McCloud, towerman after six seasons (Kingsport News, 17 Nov 1948, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Govan Smith Jr. spent about five months a year in the shelter (Kingsport Times-News, 13 Dec 1953, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Brush blaze of about 10 acres at the foot of Bays Mountain, found by a state forester on patrol from the tower (Kingsport Times, 27 Oct 1953)
Kingsport News, 5 Oct 1955: state bought a dozen 80-foot steel towers and listed one for Sullivan County atop Bays Mountain; no source found that a tower went up on this ridge
Registered 24 March 2020 as US 1401, TN 37 as the Garden Mountain Fire Tower, nominated by Don Gouge

corrections.why: The register and Bays Mountain History both give Garden Mountain Fire Tower or ET-12 as other names for this tower.
The National Historic Lookout Register lists this tower as registered on March 24, 2020; the record shows no register.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record keeps 18.3 m (60 ft) pending editor decision. The 1948 and 1953 newspaper accounts give 60 ft; the 2020 NHLR entry and Bays Mountain History give 100 ft. The story reports both.

NHLR and Tennessee Landforms place the tower in Hawkins County; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1948 paper calling it the Forestry Division's only tower in Sullivan County. Record keeps Hawkins; the story reports both.
Record's 660.2 m matches the Tennessee Landforms 2166 ft. NHLR gives 2,393 ft (729 m); Bays Mountain History gives about 2,400 ft on Holston River Mountain; the 1953 article gives 2,300 ft.

Bays Mountain History places the tower on Holston River Mountain, not Bays Mountain itself; the 1948 and 1953 newspaper accounts (as quoted by Forest Lookouts) place it atop Bays Mountain. Record keeps the Holston River Mountain placement; the story reports both.

sources.title: Bays Mountain Park Fire Tower Hike Early Arrival Experience

notes_for_editor: Height (60 vs 100 ft) and county (Hawkins vs Sullivan) conflict across sources; editor should decide height_m and county. Tennessee Landforms also lists a Garden Mountain tower (HWT001, 2405 ft, Hawkins) whose elevation is close to the NHLR 2,393 ft; possible duplicate, not verified. The record's coordinates sit about 2 km from the NHLR coordinates (36.515278, -82.623889). The 1948 and 1953 quotes come from a reprint on the Forest Lookouts page, not the original newspapers. Whether a state 80-foot tower was erected on this ridge in 1955 is unresolved. One web search used for this tower.
